newsitem.title: FRANCE: French spirits group says tax rise to cost jobs.
newsitem.headline: French spirits group says tax rise to cost jobs.

text.p: The French spirits federation FFS said on Thursday that a 17.1 percent rise in spirits tax proposed in the French welfare finance bill is expected to cut sales by eight percent and cost some 2,000 jobs.
"Nothing justifies such a brutal increase in tax on just one category of alcoholic drinks," FFS chairman Alain Trocqueme said in a statement.

The organisation wants taxes more evenly applied across the spectrum of alcoholic beverages. It said a glass of eau de vie or pastis is already taxed 32 times more heavily than a glass of wine with the same amount of alcohol.
The proposed tax increase would bring the rise in tax on spirits to 36 percent over the past four years.

The FFS said the French spirits industry employs 12,000 people directly. "Although there are several big companies, the sector also comprises around 500 entreprises, four-fifths of whom employ fewer than 10 people," it said.

"However alcohol may be consumed, it is the same product and has the same effects. The FFS is therefore stunned that spirits are saddled with 79 percent of the tax when they represent 18 percent of alcoholic beverage consumption in France," it said.
